unit_tests: [test_MOD009_dev].[test no deployed module outside the test classes references payment_source]
[test_MOD009_dev].[test payment events load still takes payment_date from settled approved cash transactions]

steps.step: re-apply after rollback matches first apply

deviations: MP-001's scope for MOD-009 says the Phase 1 procedure that loads silv_payment_events is changed to stop writing payment_source. Per the 2026-11-06 answer to Q-031, Layercake.usp_load_silv_payment_events never names payment_source (the column only took its default), so the procedure is left unchanged and the migration changes only the table. The module plan lists only Layercake.silv_payment_events as its object.

The down script re-adds payment_source with its default N'Individual', so existing rows get 'Individual'. This was the only value the column could hold, because the Phase 1 load never wrote it. The rollback therefore restores both the data and the schema.

The existing primary key name pk_silv_payment_events does not follow base standards 2.1 (PK_<schema>_<Table>). It is kept as is, because the module changes nothing but payment_source and TC-009-003 checks that the key is unchanged.
notes:
MIG-0011 drops the default df_silv_payment_events_src and then the column Layercake.silv_payment_events.payment_source (RULE-027; drop approved under Q-035 and Q-024). The down script adds the column back with its default. No procedure or view changes: usp_load_silv_payment_events already writes only the other five columns. Starting point: TC-009-001 and TC-009-002 failed and the other five passed, because the existing load already behaved as required. All 7 Tester tests and 2 dev tests now pass. The dev tests check that no module outside the test schemas references payment_source, and that the load still fills payment_date from settled, approved cash transactions (the Tester's tests leave payment_date NULL). Round-trip and checks pass. The sqlfluff findings are advisory and come from the Phase 1 lower-case style, which is kept on purpose.

Test-first: the first run had 5 of 7 of the Tester's tests passing; the final run passed 7 of 7 and 2 unit test(s), in 3 run(s).
